title: Unit tests, test doubles, TDD
idea: Testing a low-level design (LLD) checks each class through its public contract, with test doubles for risky collaborators; test-driven development (TDD) writes each test first.

analogy.text: A flight simulator. Pilots rehearse an engine failure safely because the cockpit takes its signals from software, not from a real engine.
analogy.breaks: A simulator can disagree with the real plane; so can a test double.

points: Constructor injection gives every collaborator a seam where a test double plugs in.
A stub returns canned answers; a mock also records calls you then verify.
Test behaviour through public methods, never through private fields or helpers.
TDD loops red, green, refactor: failing test, least code, then tidy up.

hero.title: One turn of the TDD loop

steps.caption: Write a test for behaviour that does not exist yet: `pay` must reject a zero total.
Run it and watch it fail. A test you never saw fail may test nothing.
Add the least code that passes: one guard clause at the top of `pay`.
Rename, extract and remove duplication in small steps. Rerun every test after each one.
Pick the next behaviour, such as "a declined card returns false", and start the loop again.

code.title: Hand-written double and checks
code.caption: `Checkout` is tested with a hand-written test double that records every charge. No real payment provider is touched.

walk.text: A tiny runner: `check` prints PASS or FAIL and counts failures.
The collaborator is an interface, so a test can swap the real gateway out.
`RecordingGateway` answers as told, like a stub, and records calls, like a mock.
`Checkout` receives its gateway through the constructor: the seam the test uses.
State check: the result. Interaction check: what the gateway was asked to do.
The bad input throws, and the recorded calls prove no charge leaked through.

code.title: Same tests in JUnit 5
code.caption: What teams write with JUnit 5 and Mockito. Mockito generates the double, so you write no double class.

walk.text: `mock` builds a `PaymentGateway` double; the real `Checkout` uses it.
Stub: `when(...).thenReturn` sets the answer for this exact call.
Assert the result, then `verify` the gateway got exactly this call.
`assertThrows` checks the guard; `verifyNoInteractions` proves nothing was charged.

pitfalls: Mock only collaborators at boundaries, never value objects or the class under test.
Do not verify every call; tests that pin internals break on each safe refactor.
If `new` builds a collaborator inside the class, inject it so tests can swap it.

quiz.q: With this `pay`, what is the last line `CheckoutTestDemo` prints?
quiz.why: `RecordingGateway` records the zero charge before the throw, so it holds two calls. Only the "never charged" check fails; the throw is still caught.

takeaway: Inject collaborators, swap risky ones for doubles, and let a failing test lead.

starters: When should I hand-write a test double instead of a Mockito mock?
How do I test a class that calls new inside its methods?
Is TDD worth doing in a timed LLD interview?
